# Fama and Macbeth Regression Analysis {#sec-bem-annual-fm}

This chapter uses BEM's annual methodology sample from @sec-summary-statistics to illustrate the two steps of a Fama–MacBeth regression.
The first step fits a cross-sectional regression in each formation year.
The second averages the coefficients across years and estimates their standard errors from the time series of annual coefficients.

{{< include _show-table.qmd >}}

```{python}
import polars as pl

from eap_pl import build_annual_panel

annual_panel = build_annual_panel()
```

## Implementation

### Periodic Cross-Sectional Regressions

Compare three univariate regressions with a regression that includes beta, size, and book-to-market together.
The outcome is the next year's excess return in percent.
Following @bali2016 [chap. 6], winsorize the regressors at 0.5% in each year's regression sample.
Use six Newey–West lags when estimating standard errors for the averages.

```{python}
import statspai as sp

specifications = [["Beta"], ["Size"], ["BM"], ["Beta", "Size", "BM"]]
term_labels = {"BM": "Book-to-market"}
fits = []
for terms in specifications:
    sample = (
        annual_panel.select("year", "excess", *terms).drop_nulls()
        .with_columns(
            pl.col(terms).era.winsorize(prob=0.005, quantile_method="linear").over("year")
        )
    )
    fits.append(sp.fama_macbeth("excess ~ " + " + ".join(terms),
                               data=sample, time="year", lags=6))
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem6-periodic
#| tbl-cap: Annual cross-sectional regressions (BEM Table 6.1)
#| echo: false

def periodic_results(fit, terms):
    result = pl.from_pandas(fit.model_info["period_coefs"].reset_index())
    return result.with_columns(
        adj_r2=1 - (1 - pl.col("r2")) * (pl.col("nobs") - 1) / (pl.col("nobs") - len(terms) - 1)
    )

periodic = [periodic_results(fit, terms) for fit, terms in zip(fits, specifications)]
show_table(pl.concat([
    frame.with_columns(pl.lit(str(i)).alias("Model"))
    for i, frame in enumerate(periodic, 1)
], how="diagonal").select("Model", pl.exclude("Model")).rename(term_labels))
```

### Average Cross-Sectional Regression Results

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem6-summary
#| tbl-cap: Average coefficients and Newey–West inference (BEM Table 6.2)
#| echo: false

rows = [
    [i, term_labels.get(term, term), fit.params[term], fit.std_errors[term],
     fit.tvalues[term], f"{fit.pvalues[term]:.3f}"]
    for i, fit in enumerate(fits, 1) for term in fit.params.index
]
show_table(pl.DataFrame(rows, schema=["Model", "Term", "Average", "SE", "t", "p"], orient="row"))
```

## Interpreting FM Regressions {#sec-annual-fm-inference}

The ordinary Fama–MacBeth standard error is the standard deviation of the annual slopes divided by the square root of the number of years.
For the size slope in the regression with all three characteristics, compare the ordinary $t$-statistic with the six-lag Newey–West $t$-statistic.

```{python}
size_slopes = periodic[-1]["Size"]
ordinary_se = size_slopes.std() / len(size_slopes)**0.5
pl.DataFrame({
    "Standard error": ["Ordinary", "Newey–West (six lags)"],
    "t": [size_slopes.mean() / ordinary_se, fits[-1].tvalues["Size"]],
}).with_columns(pl.col("t").round(2))
```

The six-lag adjustment changes the significance decision at the 5% level in this example.

## Presenting FM Regressions

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bem6-compact
#| tbl-cap: Compact Fama–MacBeth regression table (BEM Table 6.3)
#| echo: false

from eap_pl import format_fit

terms = ["Beta", "Size", "BM", "Intercept"]
labels = [term_labels.get(term, term) for term in terms]
columns = {"Term": [*labels, "R²", "Adjusted R²", "n"]}
for i, (fit, frame) in enumerate(zip(fits, periodic), 1):
    columns[f"({i})"] = [
        format_fit(fit, term) if term in fit.params else "" for term in terms
    ] + [f"{frame['r2'].mean():.3f}", f"{frame['adj_r2'].mean():.3f}", f"{frame['nobs'].mean():.0f}"]
show_table(pl.DataFrame(columns))
```
